the study of strong convergence of iterative processes for a class of nonexpansive mappings.
the convergence of the Mann and Ishikawa iteration schemes for a class of nonlinear mappings, called strong pseudo-contractions, in uniformly smooth Banach spaces.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proved the strong convergence of the Mann and Ishikawa iteration procedures for the class of strongly pseudo-contractive mappings in the setting of Banach spaces.
the Mann and Ishikawa iteration schemes are global for the class of all strongly pseudo-contractive self-mappings in a Banach space.

the Mann and Ishikawa iteration schemes are strongly convergent for a strong pseudo-convex map T, for any initial vector, in the absence of the continuity of T, in the case of arbitrary iteration parameters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in a real uniformly smooth space, the strong convergence of the iteration processes does not depend on the geometry of the space or any property of the map.
we are able to remove all continuity assumptions from the classical Mann and Ishikawa iteration schemes for strong pseudo-contractive maps in a real uniformly smooth, uniformly convex Banach space.
, in a real uniformly smooth space, strong pseudo-contractions are not only fixed-point preserving, but also fixed-point attracting.
